incident.name: PHP2Shell
incident.summary: Two CVEs covering four related memory-safety bugs in PHP's core engine that allow unauthenticated remote code execution and remote disclosure of process memory (which can contain credentials, tokens and keys). The flaws are below the application layer, so apps like WordPress, Drupal and Magento are exposed even if their own code is secure. Attackers send crafted web requests; per CrowdStrike the main server-side trace is a memory-limit error.
incident.affected_versions: Per Wiz, nearly every PHP version back to 5.4 has at least one affected bug; THN reports every 7.x and 8.x release affected.
incident.discovered_by: Wiz Research (Sagi Tzadik, Shir Tamari, Nir Ohfeld, Tomer Schwartz) with Calif and OpenAI
incident.first_known_exploitation: 2026-10-17 (single probe against Amazon MadPot honeypot, during embargo)
incident.cisa_kev: Not listed as of catalog version 2026.10.23 (released Oct 23, 19:30 UTC; the feed was opened directly at 07:08 ET Oct 26: 1,756 entries, none of CVE-2026-109618, -109619 or -115560; the newest additions are Arista VeloCloud and Collabora Online, dated Oct 23). No emergency directive found.

incident.status_summary: As of late Oct 22, 2026 ET: mass scanning and exploitation attempts (millions per Cloudflare) and multiple actors (AWS), with a Mirai-variant botnet payload blocked by Sophos. NO publicly confirmed successful compromise of any named organization; a Sophos claim of one success was retracted. The main real-world damage is the wave of precautionary outages across governments, banks, airlines, telecoms, HR/payroll SaaS, nonprofits and media in at least 12 countries. Not in CISA KEV; no CISA emergency directive.
gaps: CISA alert page, CNBC, Reuters, AP, BBC, CBC, NBC and cyber.gov.au pages could not be fetched directly; their content is via secondary reporting.

Exact x.com status URLs for the NSA, FBI Cyber Division, Matthew Prince, PM Takaichi, Minister Solomon and Minister Bae posts were not retrieved. Found: Greg Brockman (x.com/gdb/status/2112921529650688312), ThaiCERT and Rep. Lori Trahan.
No internet-wide patched-share figure captured (Censys tracker loads dynamically; Shadowserver data not found).
No ransomware gang, state group or leak-site claim tied to PHP2Shell found.

Leak source unresolved: CVE IDs circulated Oct 20 ~15:00 UTC, a pseudonymous Hacker News post, Calif's mistaken PoC video, possible leak of critical-infrastructure mitigation advice, and Chainguard's early images. How the Oct 17 actor obtained details is unknown.
Many outages (Nintendo, Asana, Duolingo, GOG, some Japanese games) are not confirmed as PHP2Shell-related.
Wikipedia article on PHP2Shell could not be fetched.

related_advisory.note: PHP informational advisory: an 'unlikely RCE vector' reachable only under an unusual combination of session configuration and application code; mitigation session.upload_progress.enabled=0 (already listed Oct 21 for CVE-2026-109619); full advisory to come with the next regular bugfix release. No exploitation reported.

timeline.event: An initial PHP out-of-memory flaw was found but left unpatched because exploitation was not proven.
The memory issue was partially rediscovered during an external PHP security audit; PHP Foundation later called the delay in fixing it a structural failure.
PHP Foundation creates an Ecosystem Security Team for triage, coordination and hardening.
Calif finds the first issue using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol under OpenAI's Patch the Planet program (per Fortune/AAP).
Calif and OpenAI independently report the out-of-memory-to-RCE issue (per SecurityWeek).
Wiz Research discovers the first vulnerability with AI assistance.
Wiz confirms unauthenticated RCE against Drupal.
Wiz confirms unauthenticated RCE against WordPress.
Wiz reports the findings to the PHP security team.
PHP acknowledges the reports and begins developing a fix (per Wiz).
Last PHP releases before the fix; VirusTotal later counted ~85,000 IPs on these builds.
White House says it learned of the flaw on 'Friday' (interpreted as Oct 16).
First known exploitation attempt: a single probe hits Amazon's MadPot honeypot from anonymized infrastructure, four days before disclosure, while the bugs were under embargo.
watchTowr publicly confirms the rumored vulnerabilities are real and says it reproduced them, without publishing details.
Modat scans the internet and counts ~4.38M PHP services on ~1.89M hosts, ~79% on unsupported branches.
A pseudonymous Hacker News user leaks details ahead of the planned disclosure (per Infosecurity Magazine and SecureWorld); the leak source is unidentified.
The two CVE IDs start circulating online with a wrong release time and an inflated CVSS 10.0; no technical details yet.
PHP moves up its pre-announcement and brings the release forward one day, from Oct 22 to Oct 21 at 14:00 UTC.
Calif mistakenly publishes a video showing a proof of concept; copies spread on social media. Mitigation advice shared with some critical infrastructure providers may also have leaked.
Earliest PoC-based exploitation attempts appear on release day; more attempts follow from other anonymized infrastructure through 08:00 UTC.
An archive with leaked vulnerability details is submitted to VirusTotal before the patch.
Cloudflare deploys WAF protections about nine hours before public disclosure.
Cloudflare WAF protections go live for free and paid plans.
Patchstack says hosting partners have reported multiple active exploitation incidents.
Chainguard publishes built images containing the fix more than six hours early; the PHP Foundation says this broke the embargo.
ELLIO records its first related request, under an hour after Chainguard's images.
Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi posts on X urging site operators to patch before the 23:00 JST release.
PHP security updates published (time per ENISA joint statement). The EU joint statement from DG CNECT, ENISA, CERT-EU, Europol EC3 and the CSIRTs Network follows.
Debian (DSA-6574-1) and DirectAdmin ship fixes alongside the upstream release.

PHP releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 plus minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1; coordinated disclosure; Wiz publishes its write-up. Recorded Future logs the fixes shipping at 13:52 UTC.
UK NCSC issues an alert urging immediate updates.
CISA publishes an alert saying the PHP flaws require immediate patching.
watchTowr's Attacker Eye honeypots observe in-the-wild exploitation attempts against both CVEs (none successful at that point).

Governments and companies in Europe, Canada, Japan, Australia and the UK take websites offline as a precaution. The largest are Dutch DigiD, the French prefectures, Germany's ITZBund, Finland's Valtori, Statistics Canada, 32 UK government services, BambooHR, Orange, Mizuho, Wikimedia and Internet Archive.
Slovenia raises its national cyber threat level to high.
OpenAI publishes 'Patch the Planet' post and releases the php2shell-checker (Codex skill).
More PoCs appear within hours and are used against AWS sensors almost immediately; hundreds of PoC repositories appear on GitHub, most fake (JFrog finds prank malware).
RHEL 9/10, Ubuntu (USN-8948-1), Docker official images, cPanel EasyApache, Plesk, SUSE, Alpine and Pantheon (8.2-8.5) ship fixes.
Acquia reports all customer applications patched.
Rocky Linux, CloudLinux, Pantheon (all LTS), WP Engine and Kinsta complete or advance rollouts.
Pantheon reports blocking more than 60,000 suspicious requests.
South Korea raises its private-sector cyber crisis alert from 'interest' to 'caution'.
VulnCheck says a weaponized exploit for CVE-2026-109618 works on default production settings of PHP 8.4.10-8.4.26 on x86-64.
Originally planned disclosure date.
Sophos retracts an earlier claim of one successful in-the-wild compromise; officials in Germany, the Netherlands, Japan and Australia say there are no confirmed breaches.
Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince says on X that attempts have reached millions.
CISA KEV: neither CVE-2026-109618 nor CVE-2026-109619 is in the KEV catalog as of version 2026.10.21 (verified directly from the CISA feed at ~23:30 ET Oct 22). No CISA emergency directive found.

Hunt.io maps attacker open directories holding PHP2Shell tooling: one operator ran ten attack rounds against a list that grew from 23 to 123 servers; about 57 ran PHP; zero shells. Hunt.io: 'no confirmed compromises, and no vendors have reported any.'

VulnCheck says it has built an exploit for CVE-2026-109618 that reaches code execution on x86-64 with ASLR on and error display off (the recommended production setup); kept to its paying customers; says it is not aware of any other public or commercial exploit that does this across multiple PHP versions.

Qualys (anonymized data from about 12,000 customers): only about 199,000 PHP instances were patched within 12 hours of disclosure; about 110 million instances (71%) run end-of-life PHP 5.4 to 8.1 and most will never get a patch; another 44 million run supported branches without the fix applied.

PHP publishes an informational advisory for a third issue, CVE-2026-115560, an 'unlikely RCE vector' that needs an unusual session configuration; it recommends session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release and will publish a full advisory then. No exploitation reported.
CISA KEV re-checked from the feed: catalog still at version 2026.10.21; neither PHP CVE listed. No emergency directive found.

The Record: dozens of experts tell the outlet no PHP2Shell attempt is known to have succeeded and most public proof-of-concept exploits work only in lab conditions; Google's John Hultquist says it has not validated in-the-wild exploitation but calls the threat 'viable and very serious'; Censys counts more than 41 million internet-facing PHP services on affected versions and about 1 million on a fixed release as of Oct 22.

CISA KEV re-checked from the feed: catalog moved to version 2026.10.23 (released 19:30 UTC) with two new entries (Arista VeloCloud, Collabora Online); neither PHP CVE is listed and no emergency directive has been issued.

The PHP Foundation's executive director, Elizabeth Barron, tells The Register the foundation has no evidence of successful exploitation of the two flaws before disclosure and none on patched versions; Mandiant CTO Charles Carmakal says it has validated some public exploits that achieve code execution against default mod_php deployments but not PHP-FPM, calls many others 'vibe-coded', and says exploitation 'may have already begun in a limited fashion'.

VulnCheck's status update: its private exploit now covers PHP 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 to 8.5.11 on default mod_php settings, including default WordPress Docker installs; the one real exploitation attempt it logged (Oct 21) tried and failed to plant a web shell, and all ten follow-up reads returned 404. Its exposure count: PHP on 2,608,039 internet-facing hosts, 99.998% of them on vulnerable or likely vulnerable versions.

Reuters: the PHP Foundation has one full-time employee (Barron) and 14 mostly part-time contractors; Barron says the foundation has no evidence the flaws were exploited before disclosure or on patched sites and has received 'no further indication from OpenAI, Wiz or Calif' of problems on patched systems. PHP now receives nearly twice as many proposed code changes as a year ago without a matching rise in contributors.

Korea's KISA (KrCERT/CC) publishes security notice #2581 recommending the temporary mitigation for the third PHP bug, CVE-2026-115560 (disable session upload progress and restart PHP workers); no exploitation of the third bug is reported.

Fourth morning after the patches: no named organization has confirmed a PHP2Shell compromise; no PHP release after Oct 21 (php.net's newest entry is the Oct 23 advisory). CISA's KEV feed could not be opened by this run; the latest readable notices show CISA's Oct 23 additions were Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud only, with no PHP entry and no emergency directive.

American Banker: MSU Federal Credit Union ($8.9 billion, East Lansing, Michigan) took its website and digital banking offline on Oct 21 after federal warnings, patched the PHP systems it builds and maintains itself and restored online and mobile banking on Oct 22, about 24 hours later; 'There is no impact to member information at this time' (chief of staff Allison Horn). New York's Department of Financial Services told regulated firms in an Oct 22 industry letter to patch immediately, take unpatchable systems offline and not treat web application firewalls as a substitute for patching or isolation. The Japanese Bankers Association said the interbank settlement network was not affected. No US bank or credit union has reported a compromise.

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 updates its PHP2Shell threat brief with the first vendor account of a successful intrusion: 'In one case, the attackers targeted a government entity in Europe' and within two hours of initial exploitation 'had successfully accessed password hashes and multi-factor authentication secrets', set up a relay into Active Directory and attempted domain-admin escalation. Unit 42 judges the command style 'strong indicators of an agentic attacker' (output wrapped in machine-readable delimiters for a model to parse). The entity is not named, the data source is not stated, and the outcome of the escalation attempt is not given. Cortex Xpanse counts more than 22.6 million exposed instances potentially vulnerable.

French prefecture websites (Nord, Rhône, Bouches-du-Rhône, Gironde) come back online at 10:21 UTC after going dark at 17:05 UTC on Oct 21, per the volunteer phpocalypse tracker, which stopped automated checks on Oct 23 with every site it had listed as dark recovered (DigiD and NCSC-NL on Oct 21; Valtori, Overheid.nl, CNIL, Belgian Foreign Affairs, NotuBiz and the Dutch data-protection authority on Oct 22). Observational, not an official restoration notice.

CYFIRMA (Singapore) publishes a report, relayed by Korea JoongAng Daily on Oct 24, that Korean-speaking actors on the I2P anonymity network are preparing PHP2Shell attacks, dubbed 'June 2026 Minjun', against government and financial institutions in South Korea, the United States, Japan and Australia, with manufacturing, logistics, aviation and trading firms also listed. CYFIRMA rates its confidence in the preparations high and a Lazarus link moderate; no victim, malware or infrastructure tied to North Korea is identified, and Korean security sources say the language and target choice alone prove nothing. Korea's science ministry and KISA had issued a 'caution' alert on Oct 22.

The CISA KEV feed, opened directly by this run: catalog version 2026.10.23, released Oct 23 at 19:30 UTC, 1,756 entries, none of the three PHP CVEs; no additions dated Oct 24. php.net's newest entry remains the Oct 23 informational advisory; no PHP release since Oct 21 (PHP 8.6.0 RC5 is planned for Nov 5). TechCrunch's Oct 24 reconstruction says Palo Alto Networks and Trail of Bits 'later reported confirmed compromises as of late Friday'; the Unit 42 case is the only such account this run could read, and no Trail of Bits post claiming a compromise was found.

Evening check, day four: nothing new. The CISA KEV feed, opened directly: still catalog version 2026.10.23 (released Oct 23, 19:30 UTC), 1,756 entries, no PHP2Shell CVE; the latest additions remain Arista VeloCloud and Collabora Online. php.net's archive, opened directly: newest entry still the Oct 23 informational advisory; no PHP release since Oct 21. No vendor research, agency advisory or named compromise dated after midday Oct 24 was found in a sweep of the security press and of Unit 42, CrowdStrike, Sophos, Censys, Cloudflare, Rapid7, Fortinet, Huntress, F5, watchTowr and the NCSC-NL repository. TechCrunch's line that Trail of Bits has 'confirmed compromises' links to an X post by its CEO Dan Guido (x.com/dguido/status/2113825891021144306), which this run could not open; no Trail of Bits publication making that claim was found.

Reuters (Raphael Satter and AJ Vicens): seven security professionals say AI-driven bug finding will keep producing weeks like this one. VulnCheck research due in the coming days finds AI helped drive a doubling of disclosed vulnerabilities year on year; Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince says he knows of 'a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities that are present in other pieces of critical software'. curl's Daniel Stenberg and ArmorCode's Ramy Rahman push back: AI-found bugs tend to be obscure and 'more disclosed vulnerabilities do not automatically mean more successful attacks'.

Morning check, day five: still nothing on the scoreboard. The CISA KEV feed, opened directly: catalog version 2026.10.23 (released Oct 23, 19:30 UTC), 1,756 entries, no PHP2Shell CVE; the latest additions remain Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator and Collabora Online. php.net's archive, opened directly: newest entry still the Oct 23 informational advisory; no PHP release since Oct 21. The Oct 25 reporting is all Asian: Korean groups saying they found no breach, a Japanese count of service suspensions, Nepal's government platform still offline. No vendor or agency published new research overnight.

The X post by Trail of Bits CEO Dan Guido that TechCrunch's Oct 24 reconstruction links for 'confirmed compromises', opened by this run: it announces that the firm's own exploit is 'now production-grade' (stock php.ini-production, ASLR, under load; ARM64 and x86-64; MediaWiki, WordPress, phpBB and Laravel; Apache/mod_php and nginx/php-fpm to root). It is an exploit-capability update, not a report that any organization was compromised. Unit 42's unnamed European government entity remains the only account of a successful intrusion.

Japan: the cumulative count of service suspensions has passed 500, per an analysis of X posts by the security firm Assured relayed by FNN's Tokyo correspondent; as of 14:00 JST on Oct 23, 285 of them (about 60% of organizations that announced a suspension) had posted no resumption notice. SoftBank's emergency-alert emails (SoftBank, Y!mobile, LINEMO) have been suspended since Oct 23 with inspections due to finish Oct 26, so users cannot receive earthquake, tsunami, disaster or evacuation information through them; NTT Docomo suspended some transmissions including J-Alert and local evacuation information but kept earthquake early warnings and tsunami alerts. Orbis resumed its online store at midday Oct 22 and re-suspended it the same day after the third bug surfaced; Bandai Namco: 'We have not yet identified the full scope of the impact.'

South Korea: Samsung Electronics, SK, Hyundai Motor, LG and HD Hyundai say they have found no breach exploiting the flaws (most of their web services run on Java rather than PHP); POSCO set up an emergency response team and patched its PHP systems, GS issued an emergency notice and updated some PHP sites, per Newsis. The reported worry is contractors and small firms on PHP 8.1 or older, which cannot take the Oct 21 patch; PHP 8.2 support ends Dec 31. Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon told the Oct 23 National Assembly audit a cross-ministry plan would follow. KISA on Oct 24 recommended a temporary mitigation for the third bug, CVE-2026-115560, which the Oct 21 updates do not cover, and advised checking for signs of intrusion as well as patch status.

Nepal: thousands of government websites, which run on the shared GIWIMS platform, and Nepal Rastra Bank's website and web services remain offline as a precaution, along with the Department of Revenue Investigation's freight-tracking system (VCTS); private banks shut digital services too, and Nabil Bank, Sanima Bank and Nepal Investment Mega Bank have since restored theirs, per the Kathmandu Post. The government's Software Development and Operation Centre expects to patch the platform centrally and bring the sites back between Sunday evening and Tuesday, after the Dashain holiday; systems not using PHP came back from Oct 22. The National Cyber Security Centre's director says there have been no cases of unauthorised access linked to the flaws in Nepal.

BBC profiles Ondřej Surý, the volunteer who packages PHP for Debian and Ubuntu in his spare time: warned in advance by the PHP project, he had to rush the packages when the leak brought the release forward, and received more than $10,000 (£7,470) in donations in a few days. 'I think this is was the most severe incident in years,' he said, adding that with AI capabilities improving in cyber security 'this might not be an isolated incident.'

First public packet-to-process evidence of the full PHP2Shell chain reaching code execution in the wild, on honeypots: a researcher publishing as 0x4D31 reports that on three disposable PHP 8.4.26 honeypots, packet captures and kernel process events correlate 35 complete execution-stage requests with 35 shell starts parented by Apache workers, from two hosting-network source addresses (OVH US, 3 shells from 15:35 UTC; Interserver, 32 shells from 16:46 to 18:57 UTC), using the published leak-guided technique; two further addresses only crashed workers. The author stresses the targets ran an 'intentionally favorable single-worker mod_php profile', that this 'is not a measurement of exploit reliability on other worker counts, PHP builds, or applications', and that no second-stage file was downloaded. A companion report covering Oct 22 to early Oct 24 found no confirmed code execution, so the first confirmed shells date from Friday afternoon UTC. Honeypots, not real victims.

CYFIRMA issues version 3 of its advisory on a suspected North Korean campaign staging PHP2Shell attacks: it says Korean-speaking operators have filtered a 216-host target set of unpatched or partly mitigated servers, lists 15 staging addresses and 21 compromised scan nodes (38 addresses in all), rates a North Korean state nexus 'HIGH' confidence and a Lazarus link 'MODERATE', identifies no organization and confirms no compromise. A single vendor's claim; no other firm has corroborated the attribution.

SoftBank resumes Japan Meteorological Agency earthquake early warnings and tsunami warnings over its emergency-alert mail for SoftBank, Y!mobile and LINEMO subscribers, halted since 06:47 JST Oct 23 for PHP maintenance; national and municipal disaster and evacuation alerts stay off until the work finishes on Oct 26, per Keitai Watch.

NTT Docomo restores its Area Mail emergency alerts in full at 20:01 JST, ahead of the early-Oct 26 restart it had announced; J-Alert, river flood forecasts and municipal disaster and evacuation information had been suspended since about 19:30 JST Oct 23 as a precaution over the PHP flaws (earthquake and tsunami warnings never stopped), per Keitai Watch.

Midday check, day five: the CISA KEV JSON feed, opened directly: still catalog version 2026.10.23 (released Oct 23, 19:30 UTC), 1,756 entries, none of the three PHP CVEs; no emergency directive found. php.net archive: no release after Oct 21 (newest item the Oct 23 informational advisory on CVE-2026-115560; PHP 8.6.0 RC5 is planned for Nov 5). NCSC-NL's alert was last updated Oct 23, 15:45, with 'one report of possible misuse abroad' that 'has not been confirmed to have actually succeeded'. No organization has confirmed a compromise by name.

Evening check, day five: nothing has moved. php.net's archive, opened directly: newest entry still the Oct 23 informational advisory on CVE-2026-115560, no release after Oct 21 (8.6.0 RC5 planned Nov 5). The CISA KEV JSON could not be opened by this run; Tenable's FAQ (updated Oct 23, 18:00 ET) says the CVEs were not in the catalog as of Oct 23, and Senserva's tracker (updated Oct 25) lists the week's KEV additions as Collabora, Arista, EG Secure Solutions, Siemens and four Plex CVEs, none PHP. Unit 42's brief carries 'Updated October 25' in its title, but its own change log ends Oct 23, 12:30 PT. The Hacker News' Oct 25 roundup adds Bitsight's count of nearly 37 million internet-facing systems running PHP or PHP-related software and names no victim. No organization has confirmed a compromise by name.

Korea: Shinhan Financial extends its emergency PHP checks to subsidiaries outside its FIRST security-monitoring system, with a checklist covering PHP use, system impact, mitigation status and schedules; Broadcom lists three affected security products (Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager, Carbon Black App Control Server, Cloud SOC SpanVA); KB Kookmin and Woori have applied emergency patches, per eToday. The same report says financial authorities found security-management gaps at 130 of 555 firms checked, mainly unapplied patches and end-of-support systems, without tying that inspection to PHP2Shell. Financial News (Oct 25 and 26 KST) reports small web-shop operators who cannot tell whether they are affected and are waiting on hosting providers; KISA has no exploitation report.

Unit 42 retracts its Oct 23 update, the only vendor account of a successful PHP2Shell intrusion. Its brief now says the attack on a European government agency 'executed in the context of a vulnerable PHP application' led researchers to believe the flaws were exploited, but 'We are unable to confirm that initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs' (change log: 'Updated October 25, 2026, at 2:15 p.m. PT to retract our October 23 update'). The agentic-AI post-exploitation description and the hunting queries' PHP2Shell link go with it; Xpanse's 22.6 million exposed-instance figure stays.

A researcher known as 'killa' wins the stealmybitcoin.com challenge, an unpatched PHP server holding a wallet key behind the flaws, at 15:47 UTC after 19.28 hours, for 0.02511679 BTC (about $2,021 at the time), and publishes a proof of concept on GitHub; the write-up notes the script was tested on a lab copy and worked in about seven of ten runs, per Cyber Security News.

BleepingComputer (05:19 ET) reports the flaws 'successfully exploited in the wild' on the strength of the honeypot capture by Adel Karimi, detection and response lead at Perplexity (confirmed code execution against Apache mod_php on PHP 8.4.26), which Expel threat researcher Marcus Hutchins calls 'by far the highest quality confirmation of in-the-wild php2shell exploitation I've seen so far'. The targets are honeypots; Dataminr's TRACE team is quoted that activity before this was 'limited to scanning, fingerprinting, and use of non-working exploits, with no known compromises'. VirusTotal estimates more than 5.1 million PHP hosts exposed, about 3.8 million with at least one attackable port open.

TU Delft's Threat Intelligence Lab publishes a live dashboard of exploitation seen by its honeypots and network telescope since Oct 20: 41,907 exploitation requests from 586 source IPs in 274 autonomous systems and 68 countries between 08:37 UTC Oct 21 and 11:04 UTC Oct 26; 171 source IPs sent code or a dropper; two IPs sent 49 requests before the fixed releases; the busiest hour was 21:00 UTC Oct 21 with 2,116 requests.

Nepal: most government websites on the shared GIWMS platform are back after central patching, the Software Development and Operation Centre says; the Medical Education Commission's site and the Nagarik app remain down and some vendor-managed sites are still offline (Kathmandu Post). Korea: KB Kookmin Bank resumes its KB Tablet Branch service, suspended from the evening of Oct 21 on the Financial Supervisory Service's recommendation (SBS Biz, 16:07 KST). Korean security press (Dailysecu, 10:54 KST) carries the Unit 42 retraction.

CISA's catalog, opened directly at 07:08 ET: version 2026.10.23, released Oct 23 at 19:30 UTC, 1,756 entries, none of CVE-2026-109618, -109619 or -115560; the newest additions are still dated Oct 23. php.net's archive, read the same morning: no entry after the Oct 23 informational advisory. Day six without a listing, a release or an organization confirmed breached by name.

statements.paraphrase: NSA says the flaws sit in PHP itself, so any server on an affected version is exposed to unauthenticated takeover. It urges patching, replacing end-of-life PHP, and taking systems offline if they cannot be updated immediately.
statements.short_quote: Cyber actors are likely to weaponize PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.

statements.paraphrase: Posted on X urging organizations to prepare for the PHP update and take systems offline if they cannot update immediately (per Newsweek and The National).
statements.x_post: yes - NSA Cybersecurity account (exact status URL not found)

statements.paraphrase: CISA's alert said it had not yet observed exploitation. It urged inventorying PHP (internet-facing first), patching immediately, enhanced logging, replacing end-of-life PHP, using a WAF as partial protection, and taking offline any system that cannot be updated right away, including unsupported versions. No KEV listing or emergency directive.
Urges UK organisations to inventory PHP, prioritising internet-facing systems, update immediately, apply temporary mitigations or take systems offline if they cannot, and check for compromise.

statements.speaker: Evan Solomon, Minister of Artificial Intelligence
statements.paraphrase: Said some federal sites were taken down on Canadian Centre for Cyber Security advice to protect systems and Canadians' data, and would be restored once patched.
Advised immediate patching, identifying third-party products that bundle PHP, and taking internet-facing apps offline if no fix is available.

statements.speaker: Sanae Takaichi, Prime Minister
statements.paraphrase: Urged website owners to check whether their public sites use PHP and to prepare to apply the fix, referencing Japan's National Cyber Office and the 11 p.m. JST release.

statements.speaker: Unnamed spokesperson
statements.paraphrase: Said the administration learned of the flaw on the preceding Friday and that the discovery shows why American AI leadership is critical.

statements.speaker: Prime Minister (unnamed in source)
statements.paraphrase: Said he was closely monitoring the situation.
Advised identifying PHP applications and isolating internet-facing systems where fixes are not yet possible; published an inventory of affected third-party products.
Warned such flaws often give attackers a direct path to a server's file system or database, and that affected versions reach back to PHP 5 (2004).
Said it had recorded no attacks on Belgian websites.

statements.speaker: Unnamed spokesperson
statements.paraphrase: Confirmed that several sites run by federal IT provider ITZBund were taken offline.

Urged updating PHP per PHP.net and taking systems offline if they cannot be updated immediately. Also said to inventory PHP (internet-facing first), watch for PHP processes spawning shells or downloading files, preserve logs, and report suspected compromise to a field office or IC3.
statements.short_quote: take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated

statements.paraphrase: Announced fixed releases and said Chainguard's early images broke the embargo and undermined weeks of coordination. It called the years-long delay in fixing the memory issue a structural failure and asked companies and governments to fund PHP security.

statements.speaker: CJ Moses, CISO, Amazon Integrated Security
statements.paraphrase: Reported a pre-disclosure exploitation attempt on Oct 17 and multiple actors on Oct 21. Said AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a patch diff into a working exploit, so defenders should measure patch windows in hours.
statements.short_quote: The time from patch to working exploit is shrinking

statements.speaker: Sagi Tzadik, Shir Tamari, Nir Ohfeld, Tomer Schwartz (Wiz Research)
statements.paraphrase: Described discovering and exploiting the flaws with Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol, and warned that AI erodes the expertise barrier to exploiting complex bugs.
statements.short_quote: complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier

statements.speaker: Raluca Ada Popa
statements.paraphrase: Said Wiz's work shows that frontier AI is a game-changer for cyber defense.

Said one of its models found the vulnerability, called it one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory, framed it as part of its 'Patch the Planet' effort, and released a Codex-based checker.

statements.speaker: Amit Serper
statements.paraphrase: Said attacks are nearly silent: the server returns success, app logs show nothing, and the only trace is a memory-limit error. Recommends endpoint behavioral monitoring until patched.

statements.speaker: Dane Knecht, CTO
statements.paraphrase: Said Cloudflare was seeing early attacks and that its WAF rules (including for free-tier customers) are only a stopgap until patching.

statements.speaker: Matthew Prince, CEO
statements.paraphrase: Said exploit attempts grew from thousands before disclosure to hundreds of thousands within two hours and millions afterward.

statements.speaker: Benjamin Harris, CEO
statements.paraphrase: Confirmed the rumored vulnerabilities were real and that watchTowr had reproduced both, without publishing details.

statements.speaker: Jake Knott, Head of Threat Intelligence
statements.paraphrase: Said nobody had succeeded yet but he did not expect that to last long.
Said WordPress.com, WordPress VIP, WP Cloud and Pressable were already protected and customers need not act.

statements.speaker: Tiffany Farriss, interim CEO
statements.paraphrase: Warned that any server running a PHP version from the last 20 years may be vulnerable and that site owners must update PHP.

statements.speaker: Spokesperson
statements.paraphrase: Said the issue affects all known PHP versions and is not specific to Wikimedia; some systems were taken down as a precaution.
Predicted mass attacks would start within 15 minutes of the patch release and demonstrated RCE against major PHP apps including Magento, WordPress and Drupal.

statements.speaker: Lori Trahan
statements.paraphrase: Amplified the NSA warning, noting PHP runs roughly 7 in 10 websites and that exploitation began before disclosure.
Issued a critical alert on the PHP core flaws, urging patching; later said it knew of no active exploitation in Australia.

statements.speaker: Senator Tim Ayres, Science Minister
statements.paraphrase: Said the outages were not a breach and described ASD-led work with international agencies and OpenAI.

statements.speaker: Spokesperson for Minister Tony Burke
statements.paraphrase: Said the National Office of Cyber Security was aware some sites were temporarily unavailable while risks were mitigated.

statements.organization: South Korea Ministry of Science and ICT
statements.speaker: Bae Kyung-hoon, Deputy PM and Minister of Science and ICT
statements.paraphrase: Raised the private-sector cyber crisis alert from 'interest' to 'caution' (level 2 of 4) at noon KST, warned ~28,000 entities, and said multi-day manual patching cannot stop these attacks, so automated response is essential.
Recommended updating to fixed PHP versions and upgrading 8.1 and older; on Oct 22 issued eight enterprise response rules, including restarting all PHP runtimes and preserving evidence.
Convened MSIT, Defense and the NIS to review PHP use and patch status.
Urged personal-data system operators to restrict access to DB admin tools and check outsourced vendors' PHP use.
Posted guidance urging site operators to check for PHP and patch; reportedly plans to inspect government websites.
Asked organisations to inventory PHP and patch fast; on Oct 22 told owners of old sites to consider retiring them rather than run vulnerable.
Asked users to apply countermeasures promptly and investigate for compromise.

statements.speaker: Minoru Kihara, Chief Cabinet Secretary
statements.paraphrase: Said no damage reports or confirmed exploiting attacks had been received.
Urged site operators to act on the PHP flaws.
Called the flaws critical, citing widespread exploitation attempts; urged immediate updates and checks of third-party apps.
Rated it critical, said multiple reports confirm large-scale exploitation, and told users to patch urgently.

statements.speaker: Thomas Caspers, Vice-President
statements.paraphrase: Said attacks were seen but none had succeeded, and that exploitation looks harder than attackers' pace suggests.

statements.speaker: Matthijs van Amelsfort, Director

statements.speaker: Elizabeth Barron, Executive Director
statements.paraphrase: Said no working exploits had been seen.

statements.speaker: Dan Lorenc, CEO

statements.short_quote: unless there's evidence of active exploits in the wild

statements.speaker: Matthew Prince, CEO
statements.paraphrase: Reported exploit attempts rising from thousands in the 10 hours before disclosure, to tens of thousands within 45 minutes after, to hundreds of thousands in two hours, then millions.

statements.speaker: Ryan Austin, researcher
statements.paraphrase: Said exploitation did not appear to have taken off widely.
Apologized for the precautionary shutdown, which interrupted payroll.
Said it had temporarily suspended several PHP-based websites and apps as a precaution and apologized to customers.
Announced archive.org was offline.
Said its website was taken offline on NCSC guidance because of the PHP issues.

statements.speaker: Unnamed minister/spokesperson
statements.paraphrase: Said 32 government services were offline and that it was working with OpenAI and the NCSC on fixes.
Advised organisations that cannot install the PHP update to take their websites offline.

statements.organization: ENISA, European Commission (DG CNECT), CERT-EU, Europol EC3, EU CSIRTs Network

Said no confirmed exploitation was known at publication, despite unconfirmed reports.

Said that, to its knowledge, frontier AI found the flaws before attackers; warned the same capabilities can help attackers build exploits quickly; committed $1B in subsidized Daybreak access for defenders; released a Codex-skill checker; and proposed a five-stage framework for AI-found vulnerabilities.
statements.short_quote: one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory

statements.speaker: TJ Sayers, Senior Director of Threat Intelligence

statements.speaker: Costin Raiu, co-founder

statements.speaker: John Hammond, Senior Principal Security Researcher

statements.short_quote: that same early warning was available to attackers

statements.speaker: Patrick Münch, CSO
statements.paraphrase: Praised PHP's handling but warned that downstream packaging by small and volunteer teams is the hard part.
statements.short_quote: Where it gets harder is everything after php.net.

statements.speaker: Dan Guido, CEO
statements.paraphrase: Said his team built a working exploit in one day with Codex, but turning a bug into a shell still takes expertise.

statements.speaker: Nils Adermann, board member
statements.paraphrase: Said there were no confirmed exploits and criticized Chainguard's early release.

statements.speaker: Kelly Shortridge, Chief Product Officer
statements.paraphrase: Said attackers are probing PHP apps and that disclosure-to-widespread-exploitation is typically hours to a few days.

statements.speaker: Jon Semon, Principal SOC Analyst
statements.paraphrase: Said Huntress had not observed or confirmed successful in-the-wild exploitation on customer systems.

statements.speaker: Juan Andrés Guerrero-Saade
statements.paraphrase: Said AI speeds up vulnerability research for defenders but equally helps attackers exploit flaws, so patching speed is decisive.

statements.speaker: PHP project (php.net news)
statements.paraphrase: Recommended setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release to fully protect against an unlikely RCE vector (CVE-2026-115560) that only occurs under an unusual combination of configuration and application code; a full advisory will come with the next release.
statements.short_quote: we are handling it in the regular release cycle

statements.speaker: Hunt.io research
statements.paraphrase: Reported attempts and staged attacker tooling but no confirmed compromises, and said no vendor has reported one; scanning hit its honeypots about 20 minutes after the patch shipped.
statements.short_quote: Big exposure, clear intent, no confirmed working mass exploit yet.

statements.speaker: VulnCheck (via SecurityWeek)
statements.paraphrase: Said it built an exploit that works against the recommended production configuration on x86-64 and that it is not aware of any other public or commercial exploit achieving that across multiple PHP versions, but expects that to change.

statements.speaker: John Hultquist (via The Record)
statements.paraphrase: Said Google has not validated in-the-wild exploitation and has no evidence of successful wide-scale attacks, but that 'exploitation may have already begun in a limited fashion and the threat is viable and very serious.'

statements.speaker: Spencer McIntyre, director of exploit development (via The Record)
statements.paraphrase: Called many of the public proof-of-concept exploits 'garbage and nonfunctional', working only in developer environments or on atypical production apps; said 'There's a significant difference between demonstrating a vulnerability and developing an exploit' and that ASLR is not a permanent barrier.

statements.speaker: Marcus Hutchins (via The Record)
statements.paraphrase: Said he had seen no reports of successful mass exploitation; that ASLR hinders mass exploitation without being a significant barrier to a targeted attacker; and that a scanner for vulnerable systems exists, so attackers may already hold target lists.

statements.speaker: Andrew Obadiaru, CISO (via The Record)
statements.paraphrase: Said the lack of confirmed compromises shows the bugs are hard to weaponize but that this will not last: attackers are fingerprinting servers for the configurations their exploit needs, and 'defenders should treat this quiet period as borrowed time.'

statements.speaker: Elizabeth Barron, Executive Director (via The Register)
statements.paraphrase: Said the foundation has 'no evidence of successful exploitation of the two vulnerabilities from Wednesday prior to disclosure' and 'no evidence of any exploitation of these vulnerabilities on patched PHP versions'; said the third bug 'can be mitigated with a configuration setting' and will get a full advisory with the next regular release.

statements.speaker: Charles Carmakal, CTO (via The Register)
statements.paraphrase: Said 'exploitation may have already begun in a limited fashion and the threat is viable and very serious'; no evidence of successful wide-scale exploitation; many circulating proofs of concept are 'vibe-coded' and cannot achieve code execution, but Mandiant has validated some that work against default mod_php deployments and not PHP-FPM.

statements.speaker: Elizabeth Barron, Executive Director (via Reuters)
statements.paraphrase: 'We have one full-time staff member (that's me) and 14 mostly part-time contractors'; called PHP 'incredibly under-funded'; no evidence of exploitation before disclosure or on patched sites; 'We received no further indication from OpenAI, Wiz or Calif' of problems on patched systems.

Recommended the temporary mitigation for CVE-2026-115560 (session.upload_progress.enabled=0, then restart all PHP workers), noting no official patch yet; servers that already applied the setting on Oct 21 need no further action.

statements.channel: Blog (threat brief, October 25 Update, 2:15 p.m. PT)
statements.paraphrase: Retracts its Oct 23 update, which had reported attackers using agentic AI attack platforms for post-exploitation at a government entity in Europe (password hashes and multi-factor secrets within two hours, an attempted Domain Admin escalation). The Oct 25 update: 'What researchers saw was an attack against a European government agency executed in the context of a vulnerable PHP application. ai_angle.finding: Calif, an AI red-teaming firm, found the first issue on Aug 1, 2026 using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol under OpenAI's 'Patch the Planet' program, then told OpenAI, which found more parts of the bug. Calif researcher Ryan Austin is credited. Calif says frontier models helped turn an out-of-memory flaw left unpatched since 2020 into RCE. Calif and OpenAI reported to PHP around Aug 11.

Wiz independently found the first bug on Aug 19 using its Wiz Atlas tool, Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz says Gemini 4 Argon contributed to finding the bug, building the exploit, detecting attacks and validating the patch. It says AI helped adapt exploits to different versions, configurations and memory layouts and helped debug failures. Wiz calls the chain near the edge of what humans could practically achieve and says what AI changed was turning weaknesses into a working exploit.

OpenAI says it led a coalition of maintainers, researchers and security providers for two months and engaged the White House, ONCD and CISA. It claims that, to its knowledge, frontier AI found the flaws before attackers, opening a 'Defender's Window'. It released a Codex-skill PHP version checker, committed $1B in subsidized Daybreak access for frontline defenders, and proposed a five-stage framework for AI-found vulnerabilities.

The PHP Foundation says AI-assisted research sharply increased reports: 15 CVEs since July 1 plus more than 100 invalid, duplicate or non-reproducible reports. It uses AI tools to validate and cluster reports (it names Anthropic's Claude Mythos, used in an earlier scan with Alpha-Omega, and OpenAI's Daybreak Red), but people make every decision. It hired an 'AI Security Engineer in Residence'.

AWS CISO CJ Moses says the time from patch to working exploit is shrinking because AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a patch diff into an exploit, so more actors can act within hours. Sysdig's CTO says AI makes 'theoretical' bugs cheap to weaponize. TLP:Black's Costin Raiu calls it an AI-powered 'race to exploit'. CIS's TJ Sayers says AI can turn complex exploit chains into practical attacks. South Korea's science minister says multi-day manual patching can no longer keep up.

ai_angle.topic: AI-assisted exploit race after the leak
ai_angle.finding: VulnCheck says that after the leak 'a thousand LLMs were immediately pointed at PHP source code'. Hundreds of PoC repositories appeared on GitHub, mostly non-functional or fake (JFrog found prank malware). Security firm Tolmo reportedly built a working exploit in under a day.

No direct evidence as of Oct 22. Cloudflare saw attackers adjust payloads in response to blocked requests, which suggests adaptive automation but is not confirmed as AI. Sophos says its own team found exploitation hard even with AI help, and reads the lack of successful in-the-wild compromise as a sign attackers are struggling too. Germany's BSI says exploitation appears harder than attackers' pace suggests.

A White House spokesperson said the discovery shows why American AI leadership is critical. Australia's Science Minister described ASD-led work with international agencies and OpenAI. The UK government said it was working with OpenAI and the NCSC on fixes.

ai_angle.topic: Context: broader AI-enabled attacks (not tied to PHP2Shell)
ai_angle.finding: Fortune's Oct 22 newsletter cites Microsoft's disclosure of 'hundreds' of autonomous AI-powered intrusions by the China-aligned group Storm-0940 using an open-source platform called Artex, but it does not tie them to PHP2Shell. No source reviewed attributes any PHP2Shell activity to AI-driven attackers.

implications.implication: Coordinated disclosure embargoes are becoming fragile in the AI era: they protect defenders only until someone else independently finds the bug, and each early recipient adds leak risk. Experts call for shorter windows, fewer pre-notified parties, and treating patches themselves (including pre-built binaries) as sensitive.
implications.who: Frank Dickson (Dickson Research); AWS (CJ Moses); PHP Foundation; Chainguard CEO Dan Lorenc ('the new normal'); Valkey/AWS's Madelyn Olson

implications.implication: Patch-to-exploit windows are collapsing to hours or minutes as AI cuts the cost of turning a patch diff into an exploit. Defenders should measure critical patch timelines in hours, automate response, and decide in advance who can take services offline.
implications.who: AWS CISO CJ Moses; South Korea's Deputy PM Bae Kyung-hoon; Sansec ('within 15 minutes'); Sysdig CTO; InfoWorld analysis

implications.implication: Disclosure dates no longer mark the earliest possible exploitation. Investigations should start from the earliest known activity (at least Oct 17) and assume possible compromise on exposed hosts, including rotating secrets that may have leaked from memory. Patching alone does not prove a system is clean.
implications.who: AWS; NCC Group's Matt Hull; UK NCSC; Recorded Future; Ox Security

implications.implication: AI-found bugs in core open-source infrastructure will keep coming faster than under-resourced maintainers can fix them. The bottleneck has shifted from finding bugs to fixing them, raising triage burden and burnout risk, and the PHP Foundation is asking companies and governments for sustained security funding.
implications.who: OpenAI (expects similar findings to rise sharply); PHP Foundation; Madelyn Olson (AWS/Valkey); OSTIF's Derek Zimmer; OpenSSF's Christopher Robinson

implications.implication: End-of-life software is the long tail of risk. Roughly 42-79% of exposed PHP hosts run branches with no official fix, so expect lingering exposure, forced retirement of legacy sites, and slow downstream patching by distributors, appliance vendors, and OT/IoT makers.
implications.who: VulnCheck; Modat; Sonatype's Ilkka Turunen; Japan IPA (retire old sites); Mondoo's Patrick Münch ('everything after php.net'); SecureWorld experts on OT/IoT

implications.implication: Governments now treat precautionary mass takedowns as a legitimate response to AI-surfaced critical bugs. They are also formalizing frameworks for AI-discovered vulnerabilities, such as OpenAI's five-stage proposal, the EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting duty from Sept 11, 2026, and questions about who receives advance warning. Detection must rely on behavioral signals because these attacks leave almost no application-level trace.
implications.who: NSA, CISA, CERT-EU, CCB, NCSC (offline-if-unpatched guidance); EU joint statement (CRA); OpenAI; CrowdStrike
